system_overview: The LinkedIn Engagement AI is an AI-powered platform designed to help users discover trending LinkedIn posts, analyze their engagement drivers, and generate new, optimized posts for increased reach and interaction. The system comprises several microservices: a User Service for authentication and profile management, a LinkedIn Ingestion Service for fetching raw post data, a Trending Analysis Service for identifying trending posts and analyzing engagement, an AI Content Service for generating new posts, and an API Gateway to orchestrate requests from the React Frontend.

services.name: frontend
services.description: User interface for the LinkedIn Engagement AI platform, built with React. It consumes APIs exposed by the API Gateway.

services.name: api_gateway
services.description: Acts as the entry point for the frontend application. It handles request routing, authentication enforcement, and orchestrates calls to various backend microservices.

api_endpoints.description: Authenticates a user and returns an access token.
Retrieves a list of currently trending LinkedIn posts. Supports optional query parameters for filtering (e.g., ?keywords=AI&limit=10).
Retrieves detailed information and engagement metrics for a specific LinkedIn post.
Generates a new LinkedIn post similar to the specified post_id, optimized for engagement.
Retrieves a list of posts previously generated by the AI for the authenticated user.

services.name: user_service
services.description: Manages user registration, authentication (hashing passwords, generating JWTs), authorization, and user profile management.

api_endpoints.description: Authenticates a user and returns an access token.

data_models.name: User
data_models.description: Stores information about registered users of the platform.

data_models.name: SearchQuery
data_models.description: Stores user-defined search criteria for trending posts.

services.name: linkedin_ingestion_service
services.description: Responsible for connecting to LinkedIn (via API or controlled scraping) to fetch raw post data. It handles scheduling, rate limits, and initial storage of raw data. It will use a background worker for scheduled tasks.

api_endpoints.description: Schedules a new LinkedIn data ingestion job.
Checks the status of a scheduled ingestion job.

data_models.name: LinkedInPost
data_models.description: Stores raw and processed data for LinkedIn posts identified as trending or analyzed.

services.name: trending_analysis_service
services.description: Processes raw LinkedIn post data to identify and rank 'trending' posts based on various metrics (e.g., engagement velocity, total engagement, recency). It also extracts and quantifies engagement metrics and provides a summary of potential engagement drivers.

api_endpoints.description: Retrieves a list of currently trending LinkedIn posts. Supports optional query parameters for filtering.
Retrieves detailed information and engagement metrics for a specific LinkedIn post.
Trigger processing of newly ingested LinkedIn posts to update trending status and engagement metrics.

data_models.name: EngagementMetric
data_models.description: Stores historical and current engagement metrics for a specific LinkedIn post.

services.name: ai_content_service
services.description: Utilizes an AI model (e.g., LLM) to generate new post content based on input from the Trending Analysis Service and user preferences. It stores generated posts.

api_endpoints.description: Generates a new LinkedIn post based on a source post and generation parameters.
Retrieves a list of posts previously generated by the AI for a specific user.

data_models.name: GeneratedPost
data_models.description: Stores the content of posts generated by the AI for users.

databases.name: postgres_db
databases.purpose: Primary relational database for storing user data, LinkedIn post metadata, engagement metrics, and generated posts.

databases.name: redis_cache
databases.purpose: Used for caching frequently accessed data (e.g., trending posts), rate limiting, and as a message broker for background tasks (e.g., scheduling ingestion jobs).

external_integrations.name: LinkedIn Data Source
external_integrations.purpose: To fetch raw LinkedIn post data for trending post discovery and analysis.
external_integrations.integration_method: API (preferred) or controlled scraping (if API is insufficient/restricted)

external_integrations.name: Large Language Model (LLM) Provider
external_integrations.purpose: To generate new, optimized LinkedIn post content based on analysis and user input.
external_integrations.integration_method: REST API (e.g., OpenAI API, Hugging Face Inference API)

implementation_tasks.description: Initialize PostgreSQL database, create necessary tables and relationships based on data models.
Ensure Redis is running and accessible for caching and task queuing.
Implement user registration, login (JWT generation/validation), and basic profile management endpoints. Integrate with PostgreSQL for user data storage.
Develop a module to fetch raw LinkedIn post data (via API or scraping). Implement scheduled background tasks using Redis for hourly updates. Store raw data in PostgreSQL.

Implement algorithms to identify trending posts and calculate detailed engagement metrics. Develop endpoints to retrieve trending lists and specific post analyses. Store processed metrics in PostgreSQL.

Integrate with an LLM provider (e.g., OpenAI) to generate new LinkedIn posts based on a source post's content and engagement drivers. Implement endpoints for post generation and retrieval of generated posts. Store generated posts in PostgreSQL.
Set up FastAPI as an API Gateway. Implement JWT validation for authenticated routes. Configure routing to direct requests to the appropriate backend microservices.
Develop the React application, including user authentication forms, dashboard for trending posts, detailed post view, and the AI post generation interface. Integrate with the API Gateway.
Create Dockerfiles for each service and configure a docker-compose.yml file to build, link, and run all services locally.

development_notes: For LinkedIn data ingestion, prioritize official API usage. If scraping is necessary, ensure strict adherence to legal and ethical guidelines, and implement robust error handling for changes in LinkedIn's UI/structure.
The 'trending' algorithm in the MVP should start simple (e.g., engagement velocity over the last 24 hours) and can be refined later.
Initial LLM integration should focus on a single, cost-effective model. Customization options for post generation can be expanded in future iterations.
Implement comprehensive logging and monitoring for all services to aid in debugging and performance analysis.
Ensure proper environment variable management for sensitive information like API keys and database credentials.
risks: Reliance on LinkedIn's API terms of service and rate limits, or legal/technical challenges with scraping.
Computational cost and latency associated with running LLMs for content generation.
Quality and relevance of AI-generated content may vary and require continuous fine-tuning or prompt engineering.
Scalability challenges if the number of posts to ingest and analyze grows rapidly beyond initial estimates.
Security vulnerabilities related to user authentication and data handling, especially with external API keys.
